articles.title: NC State’s unfathomable last-second blunder gifts Vanderbilt miracle win
articles.summary: Wolfpack fumble with six seconds left proves decisive. Vanderbilt recover in end zone for stunning 35-31 win. Commodores complete comeback from 17 points down. Call this one the Music City Miscue.
body: NC State quarterback CJ Bailey fumbled in the end zone while trying to take an intentional safety in the final seconds and essentially handed Vanderbilt a 35-31 victory no one saw coming in Nashville.
It was as improbable a finish as the Music City Miracle, the famous last-second kickoff return in January 2000 that gave the NFL’s Tennessee Titans a 22–16 playoff win over the Buffalo Bills.
“I can’t put into words what I felt.... You get one of those in a lifetime,” Vanderbilt coach Clark Lea said. “We cheated the football gods today and got away with it.”

According to ESPN, college football teams were 1,046-1 over the last 20 seasons when having the ball and the lead with 10 seconds to go in a game. The lone loss: Michigan falling to rival Michigan State in 2015.

articles.title: Union Jack Classic fails to spark on the pitch but electric atmosphere fires up Wembley
articles.summary: The Arizona State Sun Devils cantered to victory in the first ever Union Jack Classic in front of a noisy crowd – despite thousands of empty seats. You sensed that Britain’s first US college football game in nearly 40 years was going to be a very different experience when Wembley Way began to…
body: The noise came from the Arizona State Sun Devils’ marching band, who were so energetic their horns and trombones swished from left to right like air raid lights hunting a target as they played.
Soon afterwards there came a risposte from the Kansas Jayhawks’ marching band, along with more cheers from the large crowd outside the stadium.

Watching on, two relaxed police officers were taking it all in when they were approached by a fan, Ian Taplin, from Milton Keynes. “I bet you’re glad you are not at Millwall,” he told them, leading them both to smile.

It was a scene that lingered during a humdrum match, played out over a long three hours and 37 minutes. Because, even in the lulls, those marching bands never let the atmosphere drop. The Jayhawks’ band played the Beatles Twist and Shout and Cameo’s Word Up. The Sun Devils’ band responded with Salt-N-Pepa’s Push It. It made for a great – and unique – atmosphere.

articles.summary: Roma lead 2-0 after Manu Koné’s first-half double. Strasbourg fans abuse Rosenior; Salah hits hat-trick. Lautaro Martínez rode to Inter ’s rescue as the Serie A champions fought back from 2-0 down to force a 2-2 draw at Roma, in a meeting of what had been the last two sides with 100% records.
body: Manu Koné’s double had given Roma a 2-0 lead at half-time but for the second time in a week Cristian Chivu’s side, inspired by Martínez, showed mettle as the champions fought back from such a deficit.

After the announcement earlier in the day of the death of Sandro Mazzola at the age of 83, both sides paid homage to the former Inter and Italy playmaker prior to kick-off, with the Nerazzurri also sporting black armbands.
Roma raced out of the blocks as Koné sent them ahead with less than six minutes on the clock when he readjusted his body well to rifle home Nahuel Molina’s knockdown.

The champions had bounced back from being 2-0 down inside the opening 16 minutes at home to Udinese to emerge 5-3 winners on Monday. But Inter were not at the races for most of the opening period at the Stadio Olimpico as Paulo Dybala twice threatened to double the hosts’ advantage.

articles.title: Belmont Park is back: inside New York’s $555m bet on horse racing
articles.summary: The storied Long Island racetrack, rebuilt with a $455m state loan, is smaller, sleeker and designed for a changing audience. Can it create the public needed to sustain it? Henry Miller stood on the trackside apron of the new Belmont Park on Friday trying to decide what he thought of the place.
body: “It has to grow on me,” said Miller, a 59-year-old retired sanitation worker from Brooklyn’s Bedford-Stuyvesant neighborhood who has been coming to New York racetracks for 47 years. “For me, it’s too much concrete. I don’t think it’s as friendly as the old Belmont.”

He missed the familiar trees and the ivy-covered brick facades. He missed the old bar and grandstand. Most of all, he was still mourning Aqueduct, the ramshackle Queens racetrack that shuttered in June as part of the $555m experiment that has made the reimagined Belmont possible.
For the first time in more than three years, horses were racing at Belmont Park on Friday. But almost everything else about the 121-year-old race course just outside New York city limits had changed.

Inside, the aesthetic is almost aggressively modern: bright white walls, gleaming floors and long, clean expanses that feel more THX 1138 than old-school racetrack. As one Fox Sports production assistant could be overheard describing it: “It looks kind of like an airport, but it’s beautiful.”

articles.title: Brown maintains perfect record with brutal Hedges stoppage
articles.summary: Pat Brown continues his perfect start to life as a professional with a seventh successive stoppage to hand John Hedges his first defeat in front of a raucous Manchester crowd.
body: Pat Brown displayed destructive power to stop John Hedges in the sixth round and claim the British and Commonwealth cruiserweight titles in Manchester.
Brown started slowly in front of a home crowd at Co-op Live Arena but was rewarded when he got behind his jab.
A thudding left hook to the body dropped Hedges in round six and he landed the same shot moments later to wrap up victory.
An emotional Brown, 26, spoke of how "special" it was to win the British title in his hometown.

articles.title: The border is red-and-white! Chivas Femenil beat Xolos, winning again
articles.summary: Chivas Femenil returned to winning ways in a match defined by the control they maintained throughout the 90 minutes, defeating Xolos 2-0 at Estadio Caliente on Matchday 8 of the Apertura 2026.
body: The Rebaño took the field fully intent on claiming all 3 points, and from the opening moments looked to create danger in front of the home side’s goal. Antonio Contreras’ side found set pieces to be one of their main ways of getting close to the opposing net. During the opening stretch, Chivas had several chances, but the ball just would not find the back of the net. Even so, Guadalajara kept pushing, and the reward came in the 39th minute. Denise Castro was there to pounce on a rebound inside the box and send it into the back of the net.

With this result, Chivas Femenil earned an important victory that keeps them in second place in Group B with 15 points. Now, Guadalajara will prepare for another road test, as they will visit Cruz Azul next Friday, September 25, in a Matchday 9 clash of AP26 at Estadio Centenario de Morelos at 7 PM.

articles.title: Final Eagles injury report ahead of Week 2 game vs. Titans
articles.summary: After playing Week 1 with (almost) a fully healthy roster, with only Jonathan Greenard on the injury report after Eli Stowers was placed on IR, things aren’t quite so clean for the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 2.
body: Final Eagles injury report ahead of Week 2 game vs. Titans appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

On their final injury report of Week 2, the Eagles featured six players but only two with game statuses. Jalen Carter, Hollywood Brown, Cooper DeJean, and Elijah Moore all missed time during the week but are good to go, while Andrew Mukuba is questionable and Greenard remains out as he works back from the summer pectoral injury.

While there were plenty of talking points coming out of Week 1 on offense, from the big passing plays downfield, to the Eagles’ deceptive run struggles and rookie Makai Lemon’s negative passing yards, on defense, one rose above the rest: Carter injuring his wrist.

Now granted, Carter still played the lion’s share of the snaps for Vic Fangio against the Washington Commanders, playing 66 of a possible 70 defensive snaps, but he was seen at practice days later with a cast on his wrist and thus may not be 100 percent in Nashville against the Tennessee Titans.

articles.title: Warrington beat Hull KR to set up semi against Leeds as Hiku sees red
articles.summary: Warrington Wolves set up a Super League semi-final with Leeds Rhinos after a 35-12 victory over reigning champions Hull KR in their eliminator showdown at the Halliwell Jones Stadium.
body: It marks Warrington's first semi-final since 2024 after they missed out on the play-offs in 2025.
It also means Willie Peters' tenure as Robins head coach is now over after his reign which featured the history-making season in 2025 in which he won the Super League for the club for the first time.

The flashpoint of the game came early in the second half when Peta Hiku saw red for a punch on George Williams and the player advantage for Warrington eventually became too much for Hull KR to contend with.

Warrington had a narrow 12-6 lead at half-time thanks to a converted Ben Currie try, Ewan Irwin penalty and Matty Ashton's score. Hull KR hit back through a Joe Burgess wonder-try that was started by Arthur Mourgue to get themselves in the game.

articles.title: Coventry seal first PL win in 25 years at Forest amid VAR controversy
articles.summary: Coventry earned their first Premier League victory in 25 years after Jay Dasilva's winner and a controversial disallowed Nottingham Forest equaliser saw the promoted side win 1-0 at the City Ground.
body: Frank Lampard's side needed a late VAR intervention to end their long wait for victory after Forest substitute Igor Jesus saw an 86th-minute equaliser ruled out.
Referee Jarred Gillett was sent to the pitchside monitor, where he adjudged Jesus had fouled Caleb Yirenkyi before finishing from close range inside the area.

Questioned on the incident, Lampard told Sky Sports: "As you see on the replay, he has that little step on him which puts him off balance, and it's a foul...I think that's VAR reaching the right decision."

It was the second goal Forest have had disallowed at home by VAR this season after Neco Williams had a goal chalked off in the 0-0 draw against Tottenham. and Oliver Glasner said afterwards: "I don't want to talk about it, to be honest. The referee decided, but of course it's a bit of deja-vu."
